headline: Large Energy User Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill requires the State Corporation Commission to ensure large energy users, including data centers, pay their own grid infrastructure costs, preventing these costs from being passed to residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Consumer advocates, residential ratepayers, environmental groups.
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial energy users.
news_headline: Virginia Leads the Way on Energy Affordability in 2026
news_summary: This article highlights HB 1393 (and its companion SB 253) as a key measure to address energy affordability by authorizing the SCC to assign electricity costs driven by large energy users, like data centers, to those users themselves. It aims to prevent these costs from being passed on to residential and small business ratepayers.

headline: Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill mandates water utilities to report aggregated data center water consumption, increasing transparency for water supply planning and environmental impact assessment.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, local communities, water conservation advocates, Sen. Kannan Srinivasan.
news_headline: New regulations beef up data centers' required water use reporting in Virginia
news_summary: This article details how SB 553, passed into law, will require waterworks operators to categorize and report monthly water sales data, including usage by data centers, to provide greater transparency for water supply planning, especially during droughts. It notes that information on specific facilities remains protected as a trade secret.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise
short_summary: This bill requires data center applicants to conduct site assessments, including noise studies, and allows localities to require assessments of environmental impacts before approving new high energy use facilities.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data center sites, environmental groups, Del. Joshua Thomas.
news_headline: Virginia Data Center Legislation: Tax, Energy & Siting
news_summary: This article mentions HB 153 as a bill that passed, establishing a permit process for high energy use facilities (HEUF) and requiring zoning applicants to conduct site assessments examining a facility's sound profile on homes and schools within 500 feet. It also allows localities to require assessments of potential impacts on water, agriculture, and historic resources.
